accepted.evidence: Andersen prints dāni 'now' and compares RV idā́nīm and Pali idāni/dāni, explicitly explaining initial-vowel loss. Turner 1567 section 1 lists Ashokan Rupnath dāni beside the Pali and Prakrit forms.
The printed dāṇi line says 'see dāni'. It is an inscriptional spelling of the source head newly linked to Turner 1567.
Andersen prints vacana 'word' beside RV vacaná and Pali vacana. Turner 11199 explicitly lists Ashokan vacana 'order' from vacaná; the narrower document usage fits the source's instr. vacanena.
Andersen prints vaḍhi 'increase, growth, welfare, profit' beside RV vṛ́ddhi and Pali vaḍḍhi. Turner 12076 explicitly lists Ashokan vaḍhi/vadhi/vuḍhi 'growth' in the vṛ́ddhi article.

Andersen prints silāṭhambha 'stone pillar' with Sanskrit stambha and Pali silātthambha, and explicitly cross-refers to silā and thambha. Turner 12459 lists Ashokan silā 'stone'; 13682 lists Ashokan pillar forms from stambha. Preserve both lexical components in source order.
Andersen's separate dental silāthambha line says 'see silāṭhambha'; link it to the source's retroflex compound head, newly assigned both lexical components.

Andersen prints suvaṁṇagiri 'gold mountain' with Sanskrit suvarṇagiri and cross-references both suvaṁṇa and giri. Turner 13519 gives Pali suvaṇṇa 'gold' and 4161 gives Pali/Prakrit giri 'mountain'; both source heads already have these ancestors.

The printed suaga line says 'see svaga'; Andersen's svaga entry lists the Sahasram suag[e] spelling. Turner 13910 explicitly lists Ashokan svaga under svargá; preserve the source-marked graphic variant.
